title: Zonated mechanosensing by PIEZO1 controls liver regeneration.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. I checked: Europe PMC record (isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, no text-mined accessions); the publisher page (HTTP 403, blocked); NCBI elink from PubMed 42391361 (only PubMed-to-PubMed neighbours, no GEO/SRA/BioProject link); eight targeted GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) searches (Piezo1+liver, Piezo1+regeneration, Piezo1+Dpp4, Dpp4+hepatectomy, Igfbp2+liver regeneration, Nfatc3+liver, 'zone 2 hepatocytes', author 'Offermanns', author 'Wang Shengpeng'); one BioProject search; Zenodo and Dryad searches. Europe PMC's dataLinks endpoint returns only a Mouse Genome Informatics literature record, not a dataset.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the study design comes from the abstract plus an open-access commentary on it (Cell Regeneration, PMC13652991): single-cell transcriptomics, Dpp4-CreERT2 lineage tracing, atomic force microscopy (a probe that measures tissue stiffness), fluorescence lifetime imaging of membrane tension, and zone-restricted Piezo1 knockouts in mice. No methods section, no data availability statement and no supplementary file list were retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: No downloadable dataset found anywhere. The paper is paywalled with no PubMed Central full text, Europe PMC reports no supplementary files, the publisher page returns HTTP 403, and ten repository searches (GEO, SRA/BioProject, Zenodo, Dryad, China National Center for Bioinformation) found no deposit belonging to this paper. The three Piezo1-liver GEO series that surfaced (GSE298695, GSE312200, GSE314515) belong to unrelated studies, confirmed by their titles and summaries.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable, and the likely target (per-zone stiffness, membrane tension, or proliferation index) exists only as microscopy and atomic-force-microscopy measurements described in figures, not as a released column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessable; no feature table of any kind is available.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable; stiffness (kilopascals) and tension units appear only in the paper's figures, which I could not retrieve.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown, but the experimental unit is the mouse or the imaged lobule; mouse-genetics regeneration studies of this design typically use tens of animals, far under the ~1,500-row bar. No count verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem here; if the single-cell data were released it would be a few gigabytes at most.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare: there is no download to count against the paper's claims.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. Zone assignment (zone 1/2/3 of the liver lobule) is itself typically inferred from marker-gene scores, so any 'zone' label would need provenance checking that the unavailable methods section would have to supply.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper released no data I could find, so nothing can be trained or tested.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a liver cell's gene expression to predict how stiff and stretch-sensitive its position in the liver lobule is
plain_idea.train_on: Would have used single-cell gene expression profiles of mouse hepatocytes (liver cells) paired with the physical stiffness and membrane tension measured at their position in the lobule. Number of examples: unknown, no file obtained.
plain_idea.predict: Would have output a mechanical score per cell or per lobule zone, with the true answer coming from atomic force microscopy (a nanoscale probe that presses on tissue to measure stiffness) and fluorescence lifetime imaging of a membrane-tension dye.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Liver-regeneration and mechanobiology labs would get a way to read tissue mechanics off ordinary transcriptome data, which is cheap and abundant, instead of running atomic force microscopy. It stays hypothetical because the measurements were never released.

ml_idea: Predict zonal mechanical state (stiffness, membrane tension, PIEZO1 activity) of mouse hepatocytes from their single-cell transcriptome, then test whether the mapping transfers to human liver atlases. Dead on arrival: no released data.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; with no files there is nothing to size. Size was never the constraint.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a data availability statement or any repository accession — done, and it killed the project in about fifteen minutes.

verdict_reason: No data released or findable: paywalled paper, no PubMed Central full text, no supplementary files, and ten repository searches (GEO, BioProject, Zenodo, Dryad, China National Center for Bioinformation) returned nothing belonging to this study, so Part A1 fails outright. Even if the single-cell data surfaced later, the measured outcomes are per-mouse and per-image physiology, which would almost certainly fail A5 on row count.
